base: black-and-white editorial vintage documentary photograph, desaturated, high contrast, grainy film texture. WIDE HORIZONTAL LANDSCAPE orientation, 3:2 aspect ratio, much wider than tall. FRAMING IS CRITICAL: the camera is CLOSE and the subject is VERY LARGE, filling the entire BOTTOM THREE QUARTERS of the frame from the left edge to the right edge, extending past the bottom edge. Only a NARROW BAND across the very TOP of the frame, about one fifth of the height, is empty pale bright almost-white wall or light, completely free of objects. EVERYTHING IS IN SHARP CRISP FOCUS, deep depth of field, no blur, no bokeh, no soft focus. This is ONE single real photographic exposure, never a composite: every element shares the same light and grain. THE TOP OF THE FRAME IS BRIGHT OVEREXPOSED LIGHT, and the transition from the scene into that light is GRADUAL and soft, as if the light swallows the upper part of the scene: NO horizontal edge anywhere, no shelf edge, no ceiling line, no sign, no roofline crossing the top. Surfaces and objects fade softly upward into the light. THE TOP BAND IS A HARD REQUIREMENT: that top fifth must be ONE single continuous evenly-lit pale surface spanning the FULL width, bright and uniform, with NOTHING crossing it at all: no shelf, no beam, no lamp, no head, no edge of any object. It must read as smooth blank paper. NO fog, NO mist, NO haze and NO smoke anywhere inside the scene itself; only that narrow band at the very top is pale. Natural unposed body language. Brazil, 1960s to 1970s; every sign, card, notebook, photograph, uniform or object in the scene is PLAIN and UNBRANDED: no printed brand names, no logos, no legible writing of any kind; any papers, notebooks, punch cards or photographs show only vague illegible marks, never readable letters or numbers. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no emojis, no gradients, no added color, no stock photo look.
cinema: CINEMATIC DIRECTION: camera at chest height, one strong directional light source raking across the scene, deep shadows, dramatic contrast. People LARGE and CLOSE, chest up, heads at about one fifth from the top of the frame. Every person is FULLY inside the frame: heads complete with clear empty space above them, nobody cropped at the neck, shoulders or waist, nobody touching the left or right edges.
fit: COMPOSITION FOR THE SLIDE (HARD REQUIREMENT): the subject occupies ONLY the LOWER 55 percent of the frame; the ENTIRE UPPER 45 percent of the frame is a plain, flat, evenly lit surface in a very pale OFF-WHITE tone (like unbleached linen paper, hex F3F3F3), with a faint fine texture and absolutely nothing on it: no shelves, no objects, no doorway, no window, no sign, no ceiling line, no heads. That pale surface is part of the photograph and simply continues upward, staying very pale and uniform to the top edge.

images.scene: Close still of two hands meeting over a plain wooden desk: a hand in a dark suit sleeve with a cufflink TAKING a bundle of banknotes from a rough calloused hand with a rolled-up work-shirt sleeve. ONLY hands and forearms, NO faces, NO heads, no bodies above the forearms. The hands are LARGE in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall above. All banknotes are PLAIN and generic, unbranded, with no legible figures or portraits, never resembling US dollars.

Still: an old drafting table with a large sheet of drafting paper that is almost BLANK, only two or three faint vague pencil strokes, no letters, no numbers; a wooden T-square ruler and a pencil lying across it. The table and paper are LARGE in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall above. NO PEOPLE anywhere in the frame, no hands.

The owner, a man in his fifties in a plain short-sleeved shirt, seen in PROFILE standing at an old bank teller window with a metal grille, pushing a bundle of banknotes through the opening; on the other side only the hands and cuffs of the teller receiving the money, the teller's face NOT visible. The owner is LARGE, chest up, head in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall above. All banknotes are PLAIN and generic, unbranded, with no legible figures or portraits, never resembling US dollars.

The owner, a Brazilian man in his fifties in a plain short-sleeved shirt, sitting ALONE on a row of old wooden waiting chairs inside a bank, a small paper queue ticket held in his fingers, elbows on his knees, looking down at the floor. He is LARGE, chest up, head in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall of the bank continuing above.

A wooden fishing boat lying TILTED on its side in the mud at low tide, its hull fully exposed, the mudflat stretching flat and empty around it, a few puddles. The boat and mud fill the lower half of the frame; above it, a completely flat, featureless, evenly pale overcast sky that reads as the same pale off-white surface, with no clouds, no horizon detail, no birds. NO PEOPLE.

Still: a thick old wooden beam sawn through, standing on its end on a workbench, the cut face showing the inside HOLLOW and eaten away by termites, crumbling wood and sawdust around it. The beam is LARGE in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall above. NO PEOPLE anywhere in the frame, no hands.

CLOSE on a single small shop front seen from the sidewalk: a shopkeeper seen FROM BEHIND, back to camera, no face, hat on, both hands gripping the bottom edge of the roll-up metal door and pulling it DOWN to knee height in a hurry, strong wind blowing a few loose papers and leaves along the sidewalk; the half-lowered corrugated door occupies only the lower part of the frame and ABOVE the door the facade is one plain, bare, smooth pale plaster wall with nothing on it, no sign, no awning, no window, no neighboring buildings, continuing to the top edge. The man is LARGE in the lower half of the frame.

Still: a loan contract lying OPEN on a plain wooden desk (only vague illegible marks, no readable letters or numbers), a fountain pen resting on it, and placed ON TOP of the paper a car key with a small leather fob and a house door key on a ring. The desk and objects are LARGE in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall above. NO PEOPLE anywhere in the frame, no hands.

Still: a small old iron safe with a heavy door standing OPEN, and inside it NOTHING but a single folded document (no legible writing); the shelves otherwise empty. The safe is LARGE in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall above. NO PEOPLE anywhere in the frame, no hands.

Still: an antique two-pan brass balance scale in PERFECT equilibrium on a wooden table: a few plain coins on one pan, a small closed notebook on the other pan, the beam level. The scale is LARGE in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall above. NO PEOPLE anywhere in the frame, no hands.

Still: a plain cotton work shirt hanging from a single nail on a bare pale plaster wall, seen from the front; in its chest pocket a folded bundle of banknotes tucked in and a pen clipped to the pocket. Only the shirt and the nail; NO PEOPLE, no hands, no body. The shirt hangs in the lower half of the frame, its collar well below the middle; the bare pale wall continues above it, empty. All banknotes are PLAIN and generic, unbranded, with no legible figures or portraits, never resembling US dollars.

The owner, a man in his fifties with rolled-up sleeves, sitting at a plain desk in daylight, a notebook OPEN in front of him, drawing a rough diagram with a pencil (only vague illegible marks and boxes, no letters or numbers), focused, leaning in. He is LARGE, chest up, head in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall above.

The owner, a man in his fifties in a clean short-sleeved shirt, standing behind a plain bare wooden counter, both hands resting flat on it, looking STRAIGHT INTO THE CAMERA with a firm, calm expression. Behind him there is ONLY a bare, plain, empty pale plaster wall: NO shelves, NO products, NO jars, NO bottles, NO packages, NO signs, nothing on the wall at all; the counter top is empty. LARGE, chest up, head in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall continuing above.
